title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck studies automorphisms u of the profinite group \hat\Gamma^+_{0,3}. This group is the extension of \hat\Pi_{0,3} (profinite free group on l_0, l_1, l_\infty with l_0 l_1 l_\infty = 1) by the S_3 of symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,\infty}. It is generated by \hat\Pi_{0,3}, an involution \sigma_\infty and an order-3 element \rho.

As (49)/(50) on the preceding pages suggest, such a u is normalized by fixing \sigma_\infty and sending \rho to g\rho for some g \in \hat\Pi_{0,3}. Relation (51), g\rho(g)\rho^2(g) = 1, is exactly the condition (g\rho)^3 = 1: the image of \rho must again be an element of order 3 lifting the generator \rho of \Gamma_3 = Z/3. This is the analogue of the 3-cycle relation of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group.

On the previous page, the 'loop structure' condition (54) requires u(l_0) to be conjugate to l_0^p. It brings in a multiplier p = \chi(u) \in \hat Z^* and an element g_0 \in \hat\Pi_{0,3}, defined modulo L_0 = l_0^{\hat Z}.

This page argues that g_0 is in principle determined by g (mod L_0) via the defining formula (50), but in practice g_0 is as important as g: formula (62) on the next page reconstructs g from (g_0, \gamma = (p-1)/2).

Without the loop condition one could parametrize the solutions of (51) directly. By the profinite analogue of the fact that finite-order elements of a free-product-like group are conjugate into the vertex groups, every order-3 lift of \rho in \hat\Gamma^+_{0,3} is conjugate to one of exactly two classes. These correspond to the two fixed points -\bar j, -j of z -> 1/(1-z) on U_{0,3} (j = e^{2\pi i/3}), poetically the 'north pole' and 'south pole'. This gives (58):
- g\rho = \lambda\rho\lambda^{-1}, i.e. g = \lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1} = [\lambda, \rho] ('principal class');
- g\rho = \lambda'(l_1^{-1}\rho)\lambda'^{-1}, i.e. g = \lambda' l_1^{-1}\rho(\lambda')^{-1} ('adjoint class'), where l_1^{-1}\rho is the other order-3 rotation.

Grothendieck announces (59): for loop-respecting u the principal class occurs iff p \equiv 1 (mod 3) and the adjoint class iff p \equiv -1 (mod 3). Arithmetically this is the statement that the two fixed points are conjugate over Q(\sqrt{-3}). A Galois element (more generally a GT-type automorphism) swaps the two classes exactly when its cyclotomic character is -1 mod 3, i.e. it moves j to j^p.

Purpose: to obtain a clean parametrization of the 'loop-respecting' automorphisms of \hat\Gamma^+_{0,3}, a GT-like group. This leads on the next page to the reformulation \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi) = 1 with \xi = l_0^\gamma h_0 (the 'équation des lacets').
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim that there are 'exactly two' conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts is asserted without proof here. It is true: \Gamma^+_{0,3} is virtually free, so finite subgroups are conjugate into vertex stabilizers, and this extends to the profinite completion by known results on finite subgroups of profinite completions of virtually free groups. The p mod 3 correspondence (59) is announced, not yet proved, on this page.

ideas.what: Order-3 lifts of \rho in \hat\Gamma^+_{0,3} fall into exactly two conjugacy classes, corresponding to the two fixed points -j, -\bar j of the order-3 automorphism of P^1-{0,1,\infty}, parametrized by g = [\lambda, \rho] and g = \lambda l_1^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy classes of torsion in (profinite) virtually free groups / orbifold points of M_{0,4}/S_3-type quotients; 3-cycle relation in GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Bass-Serre theory); in the GT context: Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of the 'points of order 2 and 3' in the Teichmüller tower in general terms only

ideas.what: Multiplier p = \chi(u) mod 3 decides which of the two classes occurs (p \equiv \pm 1 mod 3)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on tangential/rational base points at the orbifold points -\omega; cyclotomic character mod 3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps work on GT and Galois action with base points at roots of unity

ideas.what: Insisting on keeping g_0 (the conjugator for l_0) together with g as joint coordinates of a loop-respecting automorphism, rather than g alone
ideas.modern_name: Parametrization of GT-type elements by (\lambda, f) pairs / pro-unipotent torsor coordinates

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard step in Grothendieck's own version of the GT 3-cycle relation. The two classes of order-3 lifts and their relation to p mod 3 are natural and known in substance from the GT/Galois literature. The page only sets up the notation for the 'équation des lacets'.
transcription_corrections: Line 1-3: reading is uncertain; likely 'on s'intéresse aux relèvements canoniques de tels automorphismes extérieurs donnés par (49),(50), ou des automorphismes effectifs' rather than 'solutions satisfaisant ... solutions effectifs'.

'en principe grand L_0 dans \hat\Pi_{0,3}/L_0 est déduit de g' should read approximately 'en principe g_0 mod L_0 (dans \hat\Pi_{0,3}/L_0) est déduit de g'; the superscript reads 'g_1 \in \hat\Pi_{0,3}'.
'dans un langage marquant' is probably 'dans un sens convenable' or similar (illegible).
Second line of (58): the image reads g = \lambda_0^{*\prime} l_1^{-1} \rho(\lambda_0^{*\prime})^{-1}, not '\rho^{-1}\rho(...)'.
